headline: Ship an AI-agent startup from San Francisco before the agentic workflow gold rush peaks in 2025.
why_now: GitHub and Hug Face activity around agent frameworks is at 96 and 92 respectively, with career_value at 95 and project_potential at 96, signaling a rare window where tooling, demand, and hiring all align. As an ai_engineer in SF, you are sitting in the world's densest cluster of agent talent, customers, and investors, giving you a 6–12 month advantage before the space saturates.
study: Read the ReAct, Toolformer, and AutoGPT/Reflexion papers end-to-end and reproduce one example in 50 lines of Python.
Pick one agent framework (LangGraph, CrewAI, or OpenAI Assistants + function calling) and build a single-agent tool-using app from their quickstart to a custom tool.
Study multi-agent orchestration patterns: supervisor/worker, debate, and role-based crews; implement two of them on the same task.
Learn evaluation and guardrails for agents: tracing with LangSmith or Helicone, structured-output validation, cost and latency budgets, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
Survey the SF agent ecosystem: attend one LangChain/CrewAI meetup, follow 10 active agent builders on X, and read three recent Y Combinator agent pitches.

build.title: AgentOps Copilot — a self-improving customer-success agent for B2B SaaS
build.description: A production-grade agent that ingests a customer's usage logs, support tickets, and docs, then plans and executes multi-step actions (drafts help articles, files Jira tickets, schedules onboarding calls via APIs) while logging every tool call for review. It includes a second agent that critiques and refines the first agent's plan, plus a dashboard showing tool-call traces, cost per resolution, and success rate — the kind of artifact SF startups and YC partners can immediately grasp.
stack: Docker + Fly.io or Render for deploy
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README, architecture diagram, and one-command deploy
Live demo URL with a seeded sandbox tenant
Technical write-up on your blog or Hashnode with screenshots of traces and metrics
Short Loom or YouTube demo (under 4 minutes)

publish: Post the repo on Hacker News (Show HN) and r/LocalLLaMA with a candid lessons-learned thread.
Submit a talk proposal to the next SF LangChain, MLOps, or AI Engineer Summit meetup and offer to demo live.
Cold-DM 10 SF founders/CTOs in your target vertical offering a free 30-day pilot in exchange for a public testimonial and logo.
Publish a 6-tweet thread on X with the trace screenshot, before/after metrics, and a clear 'looking for design partners' CTA.
skills: Prompt and plan evaluation with structured outputs
Observability: tracing, cost, and latency instrumentation
RAG and vector retrieval with Postgres+pgvector
API integration design (Jira, Slack, calendars, CRMs)
Startup GTM: pilot design, pricing, and customer feedback loops
risks: Agent cost and latency can spiral quickly without per-task budgets and caching, leading to demos that don't survive real traffic.
Founders chasing every new framework ship shallow demos; pick one stack and go deep to actually win deals in SF.
Reliability on multi-step workflows is still hard — if you don't ship solid evals and guardrails, a single hallucinated tool call can tank trust with early design partners.
confidence: Very high — the signal scores are uniformly in the 80–96 range and your ai_engineer profile in SF maps directly onto the fastest-growing category of startup demand in 2025.
